title: STILL PRESENT (r2): history-row substitute with different details is a 200 no-op that silently drops the typed referee, contradicting the claimed r2 W7 409 guard
location: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-rc4-3-row-actions.md | Dev Notes (Substitution guard rails (r2 W5/W7)) vs Implementation notes (Substitution idempotency)
evidence:
- **Substitution guard rails (r2 W5/W7):** an unchanged save of the terminal referee's own trio is a 400 (Art 21 route-around); re-substituting the HISTORY row with different details is a 409 — the typed referee is never silently dropped.
- **Substitution idempotency:** the SQL's CTE returns the EXISTING live successor (`how = 'existing'`) on conflict — a double-submit or re-substituting the old terminal row (kept as history) is a 200 no-op with no duplicate audit; the trio rewrite + audit fire only on a real insert.
detail: The spec's own implementation note says ANY conflict on the guarded CTE resolves as a 200 no-op; it never discriminates by detail-difference, so the r2 W7 409 for a different-details re-substitute of the history row is not implemented as claimed.
recommended_fix: Make the CTE distinguish conflict causes: identical re-submit → 200 existing; history-row re-substitute with a differing trio → 409 branded error (or gate can_substitute_referee off once a live successor exists).

title: Effective-contact rule stated inconsistently across the diff: migration comment and epic-context still document the plain snapshot-fallback that r2 W4 removed
location: supabase/migrations/20260812140000_reference_call_corrected_name.sql:14-16 + _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-RC4-context.md (Technical Decisions) vs spec-rc4-3-row-actions.md (Dev Agent Record W4)
evidence:
- The sweep and the detail payload read the EFFECTIVE name (corrected_name when present, else contact_name), mirroring the existing corrected_email/corrected_phone treatment.
- Effective contact = corrected_* when present, else the immutable contact_* snapshot.
- W4: the effective-contact rule switches to corrected-only once a correction ran (`correction_cycles >= 1`) — a cleared channel never falls back to the proven-dead snapshot (sweep helpers + webhook fallback CASE + client prefill helpers).
detail: Two shipped artifacts in this PR still state the pre-W4 COALESCE rule (fallback to the immutable snapshot), which re-contacts a proven-dead channel after a correction cleared it — the exact AD-7 violation W4 fixed. One place updated, two missed.
recommended_fix: Update the migration comment and epic-context to the W4 rule: once correction_cycles >= 1 the corrected values ARE the contact; an empty corrected channel stays absent, never falling back to the snapshot.
